program: Child trauma therapy, coordinated response and prevention
priceScope: Matched FY2025 consolidated annual cost against partial trauma-treatment benefits; not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift effectiveness.

what: DCAC provides trauma treatment for children and non-offending families alongside forensic response and prevention.
Its 2025 treatment cohort contains 624 clients, including 50 adults, rather than thousands of outreach or advocacy contacts.
The historical annual reference includes clinical health and signed caregiver household resources; it does not assign child lifetime wages.
strengths: Newest treatment table and audited full consolidated costs are matched to 2025.
Named trauma treatments, licensed clinicians and coordinated family services provide a concrete mechanism.
Internal foundation transactions, repeated sessions and recognized donated services are not added again.
reservations: Clients are not unique completed households; dose, clinical response, utility and local share remain judgments.
Full annual costs cover forensic and prevention work whose benefits are unknown in this partial treatment model.
New Justice Center funding is future capital capacity, not demonstrated current incremental care or marginal donation impact.

sections.what: Current therapy addresses trauma with family engagement and named evidence-based approaches. Assessment and acceptance precede treatment. The treatment cohort is not a claim that every forensic interview prevents harm.
sections.monitoring: Request unique treated people and households, completed therapy dose, measured clinical outcomes, caregiver disposable resources and local patient share. Separate prevention and forensic additionality from mandated public-agency work.
sections.qualitative: Insurance, public victim support and other trauma clinicians form the baseline. Sessions, interviews, trainings and repeat family contacts are overlapping outputs, not independently added successes. Statewide/international training is not automatically Denver benefit.
sections.cost: FY2025 consolidated full functional cost is $3,354,733, including netted event costs and recognized donated services; these are not added twice. It is paired with the observed 624 treatment clients. Household/treated-person uniqueness .75, completion .7, causal additionality .4, clinical response .4, utility .03 for one year and Denver share .9 are explicit judgments. Resource gains of $150 are caregiver household disposable resources after taxes, benefits withdrawn, childcare and work costs, not child wages. They require completed eligible care and a separate .5 resource-success hypothesis. Positive gains receive .5 overlap adjustment; full $40 access/time costs and process harms apply to every exposed household, including unsuccessful care. Central actual copay avoidance and external payer loss are zero judgments, not proof of no economic effect; sensitivities assess them. Already recognized donated services remain in C; external opportunity-cost sensitivity refers only to unrecognized volunteer resources. A reported treatment expense sensitivity excludes shared overhead and is not verified marginal cost.
sections.funding: Own giving page links the current Hope Starts Here campaign; no payment was made. Consolidation includes the inactive supporting Advocacy Center Foundation with intercompany elimination, not another additive charity. Public bond approval for a future Justice Center does not establish completed incremental capacity; household public-payer incidence remains a sensitivity rather than a gross grant benefit.

model.costScope: Full audited FY2025 consolidated functional expenses, including event costs and recognized donated services; inactive foundation eliminated internally. Partial treatment benefits, not whole-portfolio EV.
model.geographicAttribution: Judged .9 share inside ten-county Denver CBSA19740. Denver/Adams service anchors do not measure residence; nonlocal training excluded from treatment benefits.
model.formula: Health = (N × unique × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted duration − all-exposed harm) × local share. Completed eligible changed households jointly log net caregiver resources and full access costs; full negatives and distinct payer incidence retained. Price = 10 × C / combined equivalents.
model.counterfactual: Other trauma clinicians, insurance, public child-protection and victim advocacy without DCAC; lower coordination or untreated barriers may remain.
model.attribution: b=.4 additionality, completion=.7 and clinical response=.4 are hypotheses; observed sessions are not causal outcomes. Caregiver resources require eligible completed treatment, not referrals alone.
model.uncertainty: Utility, duration, family overlap, clinical completion, alternative providers, caregiver gains, local share and next-gift capacity remain unmeasured. Other prevention/forensic channels are unknown, not zero.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2025 annual report treatment table:624 clients (574under18,50adults) and4,796sessions. The clients are not proven unique completed households. Outreach and forensic contacts are not added to the therapy denominator.
